title: Docker 28 stops containers communicating with Tailscale network
body: I use Tailscale so containers and services can communicate with containers on different hosts. After updating Docker Engine to 28, containers can no longer communicate with Tailscale computers. Docker 27.5.1 used the host's Tailscale-managed resolver in the container, and rolling back to 27.5.1 restores communication. I expected this to continue working after the upgrade.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Docker Engine 28, my containers can no longer communicate with computers over Tailscale.
After rolling back to Docker 27.5.1, container-to-Tailscale communication works again.
N0.label: N0 Tailscale communication regression reported

symptoms_visible: With Docker 28, containers cannot reach a Tailscale device even by its IP address.
The same custom-bridge containers can reach Tailscale devices again after rolling back to Docker 27.5.1.
N1.label: N1 direct-IP failure and firewall evidence collected

symptoms_visible: Tailscale communication from the container still fails after I insert a jump to ts-forward in DOCKER-USER and remove the existing FORWARD jump.
N1_x.label: N1_x DOCKER-USER rule-move aftermath

symptoms_visible: Container traffic to Tailscale devices still fails with Docker 28 while Tailscale stateful filtering is enabled.
N2.label: N2 Tailscale stateful-filtering setting confirmed

symptoms_visible: After setting Tailscale stateful filtering to false and upgrading to Docker 28, my containers can communicate over Tailscale normally.
The default Docker 28 configuration still loses Tailscale connectivity if stateful filtering remains enabled.
N3.label: N3 configuration interaction reproduced

symptoms_visible: I've upgraded to Docker 28.0.1; I haven't re-tested the Tailscale forwarding yet.
N4.label: N4 Docker 28.0.1 verified on affected hosts (fix applied, unverified)

symptoms_visible: Containers can communicate over the affected forwarded network paths after updating to Docker 28.0.1.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does communication fail when you use the Tailscale IP directly instead of a hostname?
Can a container ping or otherwise connect to a Tailscale device by IP?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. One of my metrics nodes was already using only the Tailscale IP and that stopped working too. I also cannot ping a Tailscale device from inside a container on Docker 28; it works on 27.5.1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Direct connections to the Tailscale IP work; only Tailscale hostnames fail to resolve.
Ping fails by IP, but the same failure is reproduced with a TCP connection instead of ICMP.

question_patterns: Are the affected containers using Docker's default bridge or a user-defined bridge?
Can you share the affected network configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I use a custom bridge network named traefik. It has IPv4 subnet 172.18.0.0/16 and IPv6 subnet fd6b:7060:8f07::/64.

question_patterns: Can you provide iptables -nvL output from Docker 28 after attempting a failed Tailscale connection?
Please capture the FORWARD, DOCKER and ts-forward chains with packet counters on the failing Docker 28 setup.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After trying failed connections on Docker 28, my dump has DOCKER-USER first in FORWARD, followed by Docker's established-traffic, isolation and DOCKER jumps, with ts-forward later in the path. The DOCKER and ts-forward chains both have packet counters. I also pasted a 27.5.1 dump where communication works.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failed packets never increment any FORWARD, DOCKER, or ts-forward counters; they stop before reaching the host firewall.
The same rule ordering appears, but the packet counters differ because I generated more test traffic.

edges.comment: The direct-IP observation came from the reporter, while the custom-bridge configuration and detailed Docker 28/27.5.1 iptables dumps came from another affected Tailscale user. All affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Move Tailscale's ts-forward jump into DOCKER-USER so Tailscale processes forwarded packets before Docker's other forwarding rules.
solution.concrete_example: Run `iptables -I DOCKER-USER -j ts-forward` and `iptables -D FORWARD -j ts-forward`, then retry the container-to-Tailscale connection.

edges.comment: This exact rule move was tried by an affected Tailscale user and did not restore connectivity. It must not be presented as the complete fix.

question_patterns: Is Tailscale stateful filtering enabled on the affected node?
Can you check the Tailscale stateful-filtering setting?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, stateful filtering was enabled on my node. I did not enable it by hand; this installation had passed through a Tailscale version where it was enabled by default.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Stateful filtering is already false on the failing node.
Stateful filtering is enabled, but I set it explicitly rather than inheriting it from an older Tailscale installation.

edges.comment: The engineer reproduced the failure by enabling this option after reading the firewall dumps. The user supplies only the setting actually present on the affected installation.

question_patterns: Can you run `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false`, upgrade to Docker 28, and retest?
Please disable Tailscale stateful filtering temporarily and report whether Docker 28 container traffic works.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I disabled it with `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false`, upgraded to Docker 28, and everything is running fine. Container communication over Tailscale works again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Container communication still fails after setting stateful filtering to false.
It works with stateful filtering false after restarting Tailscale and Docker.

edges.comment: This is a handler-initiated configuration-toggle probe, so it remains clarification_only even though disabling the setting is also a workaround. Tailscale introduced the setting as a security mitigation, so disabling it should not be treated as an unconditional permanent fix.

solution.intent: Update to Docker 28.0.1 or later, which restructures Docker's forwarding rules to avoid the Docker 28.0.0 ordering conflict with Tailscale and other pre-existing firewall rules; use disabling Tailscale stateful filtering only as a security-aware temporary workaround.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade Docker Engine from 28.0.0 to 28.0.1 or later. Docker 28.0.0's firewall refactor interacted badly with existing FORWARD/ts-forward ordering when Tailscale stateful filtering was enabled. Until the update can be installed, `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false` restores connectivity in this setup, but review the TS-2024-005 security implications before relying on that workaround.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer inferred from the raw iptables counters, rule order, local reproduction with `tailscale set --stateful-filtering`, and the successful toggle probe that Docker 28.0.0's forwarding-rule refactor conflicted with Tailscale's stateful ts-forward processing. Mapping the broader issue to the Docker firewall-chain fixes in PRs 49518 and 49538 is engineer-side analysis, not something the reporter supplied.

edges.comment: Reshaped (rule 4d): the fix is proposed here on pre-fix evidence; verification moves terminal-side.

question_patterns: Please upgrade to the latest Docker patch release and tell me whether container-to-Tailscale traffic works.
After upgrading, could you re-run your forwarding test and report the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I applied Docker 28.0.1 to an affected host and its container routing works again. On the other affected hosts, 28.0.1 also restored connectivity without manually changing iptables.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Docker 28.0.1 still has the same forwarding failure on the affected host.

edges.comment: Post-fix verification (neutral patterns; the fix is not named to the user).

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as a Docker 28 firewall/FORWARD rule-ordering regression interacting with Tailscale stateful filtering, not a DNS resolver regression; direct Tailscale-IP traffic failed too.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the Docker 28 versus 27.5.1 behavior, the iptables rule/counter evidence, confirmation that stateful filtering was enabled, and the successful stateful-filtering toggle probe.
Must recommend Docker 28.0.1 or later as the durable fix; disabling Tailscale stateful filtering may be offered only as a temporary workaround with acknowledgement of its security implications.
Must not present moving ts-forward into DOCKER-USER as the complete fix, because that exact attempt was tried and did not restore connectivity.
Must not recommend indiscriminately flushing firewall chains or permanently deleting Docker's protective DROP rules.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after an affected user verifies forwarding on Docker 28.0.1 or later.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Docker and Tailscale operator. Comfortable upgrading and downgrading Docker, running Tailscale CLI commands, testing direct IP connectivity, and sharing network and firewall configuration; detailed iptables evidence from another affected operator is folded into the same simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and practical. Revises the initial DNS theory when direct-IP evidence contradicts it, follows diagnostic instructions, and reports exact commands and outcomes.
